answer: Social-graph verification is one concrete defense: each new account must be vouched for by several unconnected existing members, and the endorsement graph is scanned for dense clusters. A sybil ring shows up like footprints circling the same dune, while genuine users sit in open, diverse neighborhoods. Flagged clusters lose standing, so clones find no cheap haven: each fake identity needs endorsements from unrelated reputable members, and endorsers burn reputation if caught. One detected ring smolders like an ember through every account it touched.
